decision: Reference for limits of calibrated first-order modeling; no outline expansion or new benchmark claim.
findings: Layers use compute FLOPs or embedding lookup bytes divided by calibrated throughput; a dependency graph then forms compute/communication streams. Validate serialized and overlapped execution separately.

Section IV assumes model parameters fit on devices after sharding; CPU/device weight shuffling is unsupported. Host-device data loading is assumed largely overlapped. These assumptions exclude the book’s offload and many CPU/GPU co-execution examples.

Compute/HBM utilization and effective collective bandwidth are calibrated inputs, not solely vendor peak specifications. The paper’s compute utilization / SM utilization / occupancy terminology must not be copied as an equality or converted into a universal MFU.
All2All and AllReduce timing depends on sharding, system hierarchy and empirical effective bandwidth. Separate streams do not establish that every real implementation is contention-free.

Figure 9 illustrates backward weight AllGather prefetch overlapping another layer’s gradient compute. Reported overlap rates belong to the particular measured and modeled LLaMA configuration, not a universal guarantee.

Table I and Figure 8 expose multiple validation targets. The reported average modeling accuracy does not establish a per-point error bound; Figure 8 has visibly differing measured/predicted MFU pairs. No figure values digitized or performance claims adopted.

Table II includes a hypothetical 1.8T LLM-MoE with 16 experts / top-2, not a published model architecture to substitute for current V4/Kimi. Table I’s LLaMA-70B label and Table II’s LLaMA 65.2B / LLaMA2 70B labels are retained rather than silently merged.

Table III reports aggregate system bandwidths and distinguishes TB/s from Tbps. Do not divide per-rank bytes by an aggregate system total. Table I and prose differ slightly on DLRM-B prediction (3.06 versus 3.05 MQPS); neither number is used in the outline.
